method: Evidence packs only, no browser, no code. Read the three home digest.md, desktop-fold.png and sheet-desktop.png at full size. For turn 2 the three motion-sheet.png, ref-0019-works and ref-0019-about sheet-desktop.png and ref-0020-release sheet-desktop.png were combined into one image and read at reduced resolution (about 650px wide), so fine detail there was not verified. The three mobile-fold.png were NOT viewed (tool budget); mobile judgments rest only on the digests' inspector findings. Motion is judged from frame strips and measured numbers, not from watching it live; page transitions were not measured. Tool calls: 12 including the write, one over the brief's 'under 12', because turn 1 alone needed 7 reads.

ref-0018.business: SquadEasy: B2B employee-engagement app (step and mobility challenges, team challenges, charity donations and CO2 tracking, social wall, brand-coloured white label) sold to HR teams; conversion is 'Request a demo'.

reasons.clarity: The H1 ('You've never been so close to bringing your employees closer together') is a wordplay that names neither the product nor the buyer; the category only appears at 18% ('Employees' favourite team-building app') and the mechanics (steps, CO2, challenges) only at 61%. The team member's 'could not name the category' is the direct result. The demo CTA is clear and high-contrast (lime pill).
reasons.distinctiveness: Cut-out tilted employee portraits orbiting a heavy grotesque headline, pink highlight words, and a rotating set of flat pastel section grounds (sand, sky blue, lilac, lime) give a recognisable, friendly identity. But it is the common 'playful SaaS' kit of 2023-2025 (giant black caps + floating photo cut-outs + stats counters); nothing in it belongs to team challenges specifically.
reasons.craft: Smooth scroll (59.8 fps, no long frames) and a consistent sticky nav, but measurable faults: H1 runs 5 lines on desktop and 7 on mobile; the pink key words are 1.87:1 contrast; CLS 0.241 desktop / 0.305 mobile; Epilogue declared but never loaded; 6 typefaces and 12 sizes; 9 chromatic colours; the hero is a 100%-height fixed panel; counters read '0 %' in the text layer and 2 stay hidden under reduced motion; cookie banner in French on the English page covers the lower-left of every screen.

claims.claim: Excellent scrollcraft: every scroll moves frames and builds a harmony of elements
claims.evidence: Motion strip confirms continuous motion: the hero fades/blurs into a phone mock-up, photos re-arrange per section, counters tick, 9 endless loops run. It is smooth (59.8 fps). But 'excellent' overstates it: the motion is mostly decorative drift and fade (opacity/transform/filter), with no pause control for 9 loops (3 with text), counters that read 0 to reduced-motion users, and CLS 0.24-0.31. Busy rather than orchestrated.
Centered headline + side cut-outs is a simple, legible scheme on desktop, but headlines wrap 4-8 lines on mobile and the full-height fixed hero plus cookie card cover part of every screen.
Inventory: 9 chromatic colours (sand, sky, lilac, lime, mint, pink, green, etc.) across text and backgrounds; flagged too-many-colours. It reads cheerful, not simple.

claims.verdict: true, and it is a page fault, not a reader fault
claims.evidence: No 'what it is' line above the fold; the category word ('team-building app') sits at 18% of page height.
With a vague H1, a 1.87:1 key phrase, hidden counters and CLS over 0.25 on mobile, this is a 6 visual and a 6-6.5 ship by our calibration.

motion.what: Floating tilted employee portraits around the hero, drifting on load
Hero headline blurs/fades out while a phone mock-up with the app feed rises in
motion.message it carries: 'here is the actual product' (the first time the app is shown)

motion.what: Stat counters ticking up (users, productivity, customers, CO2, euros)
motion.message it carries: proof figures, but they rest at '0' in the text layer and stay hidden under reduced motion
motion.verdict: decoration as built (breaks the proof it is meant to carry)

motion.what: Endless marquee loops of feature labels (A social app / Measure your impact / Move for your health...)
motion.message it carries: none beyond listing features; no pause control

motion.what: Photo collages shuffling per section on scroll

problems: The H1 is a pun that hides the category and the buyer; say 'team challenge app for companies' above the fold
Accessibility: pink highlight words at 1.87:1, counters hidden under reduced motion, 9 endless loops without pause, CLS 0.305 on mobile
System sprawl: 6 typefaces (one never loads), 12 sizes, 9 chromatic colours, French cookie banner on the English page
keep: Real employee portraits as tilted cut-outs around the headline: makes a B2B HR product feel human and social at a glance
Hero-to-phone hand-off on the first scroll: moves the reader from promise to product in one gesture
One loud action colour (lime pill) reserved for the demo CTA: the conversion target is unmistakable

ref-0019.business: Figure Film: London production company / directors' collective making commercials, music films (Boiler Room) and content; the site is a showreel-first portfolio whose job is to make brands and agencies get in touch (hello@ email, 'Let's collaborate').

reasons.clarity: For its audience (agencies and brands who judge by the work) a full-bleed film still plus 'See showreel' is the right first message. But the one sentence saying what they are sits at 12px in the bottom-right corner, there is no H1, the opening text is a row of aspect ratios, and the home shows only 7 featured titles with no client logos or credits visible in the fold.
reasons.distinctiveness: Owned concept: the hero is cut by thin vertical guide lines labelled with cinema aspect ratios (2.76:1, 2.39:1 ... 1:1), the wordmark is chopped into film-frame/gate shapes (blank rectangles, a squashed 'RE', overline bars like a film strip), PT Mono reads as a camera slate or timecode. Palette is three flat values (cream #fcf8c9, cobalt #2c54c7, near-black) over graded footage. It is pure film-craft vocabulary, impossible to transplant to another trade.
reasons.craft: Typography and palette discipline is excellent (2 families, 3 colours). Execution faults are serious: CLS 1.088 (very high), 16 project titles never become visible during a full scroll and stay hidden under reduced motion, 9-12px text, no H1, 12 sub-24px tap targets on mobile, 50.6 fps with a 33 ms p95 frame (heaviest of the three).

claims.evidence: Aspect-ratio grid lines with labels, frame-cut wordmark and slate-mono type are specific to filmmaking; recurring on all three pages.

Cream on cobalt/black with a condensed display face and mono body reads 70s film-title/print; layout is sparse. 'Vintage' comes from type and palette, not from texture: no grain overlays visible in the sheets.
Three flat colours; 7 gradients in the inventory; effects are footage grading, the frame-guide lines and width/flex-basis transitions on work tiles.

claims.claim: Explore the other pages for the pattern
claims.evidence: Works and About repeat: the same frame-cut FIGUREFILM wordmark header, cobalt fields, cream condensed caps over footage ('Marriott x Al Maha', 'Post-production', 'Our people'), split 'WHAT  WE  DO' / 'OUR  PEOPLE' headings echoing the split wordmark, and the identical black 'Let's collaborate' footer. Works is a mosaic of tiles of varied size and ratio, i.e. the aspect-ratio idea becomes the grid.

claims.verdict: visual too low, ship too high
claims.evidence: Visual identity is the strongest of the batch (9 on distinctiveness), but CLS 1.088, never-visible titles and hidden-under-reduced-motion text make 8.2 ship optimistic; about 6.5 until those are fixed.

motion.what: Full-bleed footage cycling in the hero behind the ratio grid (cuts between clips in the load frames)
motion.message it carries: 'this is our work', the showreel itself

motion.what: Work tiles growing in width/flex-basis on hover/scroll (works page mosaic)
motion.message it carries: 'pick a film', previews the frame of each project

motion.what: Project titles revealed on scroll (16 never fired in the capture)
motion.message it carries: intended to name each project; as built it hides them

motion.what: Small cream dot cursor/marker on the cobalt section

problems: Reveal bugs: 16 project titles never visible, also hidden under reduced motion; CLS 1.088
Information is too small: 9-12px mono text, no H1, the positioning sentence tucked into a corner, sub-24px tap targets on mobile
Home shows little proof: no client names or credits beyond 7 titles; 'See showreel' and the email are the only actions
keep: Aspect-ratio guide lines with labels over the hero: tells a filmmaker's audience 'we think in frames' without a word of copy
Wordmark cut into film-gate shapes and reused as the header on every page: identity and navigation in one
Three-colour system (cream, cobalt, black) over graded footage: lets very different client films sit together as one house style
Split headings ('WHAT  WE  DO', 'OUR  PEOPLE') echoing the split wordmark: one typographic gesture repeated across pages builds a system

ref-0020.business: COVEO: one-person audio/visual music project (Connell McCarthy) with 11 instrumental releases 2018-2025; the site is an artist portfolio and discography where visitors preview tracks, plus licensing and press-kit links.

reasons.clarity: Fold says it in one look: artist avatar, 'COVEO / An audio/visual project', an arc of the 11 cover artworks, 'The art of sonic and visual storytelling'. The discography is a clean numbered list (001-011) with date, format, length and a Preview button. Weakness: no 'listen on' streaming links or primary action visible; licensing and press kit are only in the footer.
reasons.distinctiveness: The arc of tilted rounded cover tiles around a central avatar, a huge faint script word behind ('these are my stories'), and a serif italic 'Storytelling' against small Inter caps form a quiet, gallery-like signature tied to the music (each cover is a release). Later sections place hardware photos (speakers, synth) as cut-outs and an orange COVEO poster: personal and coherent.
reasons.craft: Smooth (59.9 fps), CLS 0, pause control present, a single accent colour (orange). But type is far too small (8.4px tagline, 9.6-12px running text), 38 images without alt, 7 text elements hidden under reduced motion, the credits panel stays fixed over 29% of the screen in every capture, and a '{TRACK.TITLE}' template placeholder leaks into the text layer. Inter as the only working face is flagged system-font-only.

claims.claim: Music; simple, not loud, plays with simple elements (text and images) and small motions
claims.evidence: Neutral grey #eeeeee ground, one orange accent, covers + type only; motion is gentle drift of the cover arc and fades (but 37 elements move with no input at the top, so 'small' means low amplitude, not few).
Numbered discography with metadata and preview reads like a catalogue of works; the release page repeats the pattern (title, cover, video, track list).

claims.claim: Few contents and lots of white space
claims.evidence: 4618px page, wide margins, one idea per screen; the cost is that the text is shrunk to 8-12px instead of kept readable within the white space.

claims.claim: Photos not monotonous, slight diagonal tilt
claims.evidence: Covers in the arc are each rotated to follow the curve and vary in palette (sky, night street, rose, polaroid); hardware cut-outs further down are also angled.
Visual 8 is defensible. Ship 8.5 ignores 8.4px text, 38 missing alts, hidden text under reduced motion, a leaked template placeholder and a persistent credits panel; about 7.

motion.what: Arc of cover artworks drifting/rotating around the avatar on load
motion.message it carries: 'here is the whole body of work', each tile is a release; the arc makes a catalogue feel like a constellation

motion.what: Large faint script 'these are my stories' stroke-drawn behind the hero (strokeDashoffset)

motion.message it carries: lets the visitor hear the product on the page

motion.what: Hardware photo cut-outs and the orange COVEO poster sliding in on scroll
motion.message it carries: the studio and the maker behind the music

motion.what: Smooth-scroll libraries (Lenis, Locomotive) on a short page

problems: Text far below readable size (8.4-12px running text) on a page with plenty of space
Accessibility: 38 images without alt (the covers are the content), 7 text elements hidden under reduced motion, a credits panel fixed over 29% of the screen
No primary action for the business: no streaming/'listen on' links near the top; licensing and press kit buried in the footer; '{TRACK.TITLE}' placeholder leaks
keep: Cover arc around the artist avatar: shows the entire catalogue and the person in one frame
Numbered discography rows (001-011) with date, format, duration and Preview: turns a list of singles into a navigable archive
One accent colour (orange) on a neutral ground: lets the varied cover art carry the colour
Serif italic display word against tiny sans caps: a cheap, strong contrast that reads 'artist' rather than 'brand'
